data.title: Altria, Imperial Brands Merger Could Face U.S. Antitrust Concerns — Market Talk
data.description: A merger between Altria and Imperial Brands is likely to face U.S. antitrust concerns as the combined company would have over a 50% market share, Citi's Simon Hales and Sunny Wadhwani write. However, selling Imperial's U.S. combustible cigarette assets to a third party--such as Japan Tobacco--could resolve the issue. "There is considerable strategic logic for a deal from Altria's standpoint as it would diversify its footprint and provide it with much needed scale in NGPs," the analysts say. Citi has a neutral rating on Altria's stock and a $72.00 target price. Altria's shares closed Wednesday at $76.28 and U.S. markets were closed Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday. Imperial Brands' shares closed 13% higher at 34.32 pounds on Thursday, marking their highest price since July 2017. (ian.walker@wsj.com)

data.title: South African rand strengthens on precious metals rally
data.description:
The South African rand strengthened in early trade on Friday, supported by a rally in precious metals, although risk appetite was limited.

  • At 0726 GMT the rand traded at 17.3701 against the dollar , about 1% up from its previous close

  • Gold prices, a major support for South Africa's export sector, rebounded from a more than one-year low on Friday, while platinum gained nearly 5%

  • "The rand has started Friday on the front foot...as a recovery in tech and AI-related shares and stronger precious metal prices offer some relief," said Wichard Cilliers, head of Market Risk at TreasuryONE

  • With the dollar near a 22-month high and markets expecting a December Fed rate hike, he said risk sentiment was fragile and the rand was likely to stay volatile in the coming weeks

  • On the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, the Top-40 index was last up 2.2% in early trade

  • South Africa's benchmark 2035 government bond (ZAR2035=) was slightly firmer in early deals, as the yield fell 3 basis points to 8.67%

data.title: South Korean shares end week higher on hopes of policy support
data.description:
Key points:
  • KOSPI rises, foreigners net buyers
  • Korean won strengthens against dollar
  • South Korea benchmark bond yield rises
  • For the midday report, please clicknL2N47801P

Round-up of South Korean financial markets:

** South Korean shares rose more than 4% on Friday to end a week of heightened volatility with gains, supported by hopes of policy measures to stabilise the market.

** The benchmark KOSPI closed up 204.47 points, or 4.34%, at 4,915.68.

** For the week, it rose 0.9%, after dropping 7.9% last week.

** Earlier this week, the KOSPI hit the lowest level since mid-January on persistent worries about a slowdown in the global AI investment boom, prompting policymakers to consider deploying market stabilisation funds.

** South Korea's finance minister, Lee Hyoung-il, again vowed on Friday to remain prepared to take necessary measures depending on market conditions.

** "Hopes of financial authorities rolling out market stabilisation funds had upward pressure on the stock market," said Lee Kyoung-min, an analyst at Daishin Securities.

** "We believe that the Securities Market Stabilization Fund could be revised up to 20-40 trillion won, versus the current 10.76 trillion won ($8.01 billion)," Citi economist Kim Jin-wook said, expecting the fund to be utilised as early as next month.

** Chipmaker Samsung Electronics rose 4.55%, while peer SK Hynix gained 5.41%.

** Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution climbed 4.80%, while Hyundai Motor and sister automaker Kia Corp were up 3.86% and up 1.07%, respectively.

** Of the total 908 traded issues, 783 shares advanced, while 109 declined.

** Foreigners were net buyers of shares worth 1.1 trillion won ($822.68 million).

** The won was quoted at 1,336.6 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform , 0.55% higher than its previous close at 1,343.9.

** The most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond yield (KR3YT=RR) rose by 6.1 basis points to 3.687%, while the benchmark 10-year yield rose by 2.2 basis points to 3.798%.

($1 = 1,337.1000 won)

data.title: Europe before the bell: Black Friday bargain hunting
data.description:
EUROPE BEFORE THE BELL: BLACK FRIDAY BARGAIN HUNTING

The bounce back in equity markets is set to continue on Friday with Euro STOXX 50 futures up 0.6%, building on the previous day's 2% gain in the cash index.

Asia stocks are also firmly higher and US futures are well into the green as well, with dip buyers stepping in after steep midweek selling extended last week's rout.

There was no particular catalyst for the gains. It looks like Black Friday bargain hunting, appropriately enough, so the question is how long it can be sustained.

Providing a further impetus on Friday was China, where onshore bluechips gained over 4% after Premier Li Qiang chaired a State Council meeting that called for a bigger role by "national team" investors to stabilise a falling stock market.

Futures were already higher before the news, but it is unlikely to do any harm to parts of the European market like luxury that are exposed to Chinese consumer sentiment.

Hong Kong-listed big tech jumped 6%.

Away from the macro news, there is some deal news.

Infrastructure investor I Squared Capital is in advanced talks to buy German outdoor advertising group Stroeer , reviving discussions that stalled earlier this year, Reuters reported, citing two people familiar with the matter.

And traders will also have a fuller chance to react to late Thursday's story from Bloomberg that German software giant SAP is considering cutting at least 10,000 jobs in an AI-driven restructuring.

data.title: French economy contracts 0.2% in third quarter
data.description:
France's economy contracted by 0.2% in the third quarter, final data from statistics office INSEE showed on Friday, more than the preliminary estimate for a 0.1% decline.

The contraction in the euro zone's second-largest economy was also below the average forecast of -0.1% in a Reuters poll of 22 economists.

data.title: SAP Says No Decisions Made on Job Cuts as AI Reshapes Landscape
data.description:
By Dominic Chopping

SAP said it is continuously reviewing how its organization and workforce need to evolve as artificial intelligence rapidly reshapes the business environment, but that no decisions have been made on restructuring or job cuts.

A spokesperson for the German business-software group made the comments after Bloomberg reported, citing unnamed sources, that the company was exploring at least 10,000 job cuts in response to the accelerating AI shift.

Bloomberg reported that discussions were continuing, and that the restructuring could affect at least 9% of the group's global workforce, although the total number of jobs hadn't yet been finalized.

The SAP spokesperson said job roles and functions would naturally change over time, but beyond that, no decisions had been made regarding any further measures.

"We do not comment on speculation," the spokesperson said.

data.title: EQT to Buy Majority Stake in Specialty European Pharmaceutical Group Kelso Pharma
data.description:
(07:03 GMT) *EQT to Buy Majority Stake in Specialty European Pharmaceutical Business Kelso Pharma
(07:04 GMT) *EQT Agrees to Buy Majority Stake in Kelso Pharma From Healthcare Investment Firm Apposite Capital
(07:05 GMT) *EQT: Kelso Pharma Has Portfolio of Medicines Mainly for Endocrine, Gastrointestinal, Central Nervous System Conditions
(07:35 GMT) EQT to Buy Majority Stake in Specialty European Pharmaceutical Group Kelso Pharma

By Dominic Chopping

Swedish buyout group EQT said it agreed to acquire a majority stake in specialty pharmaceutical group Kelso Pharma from healthcare-investment firm Apposite Capital.

Founded in 2021, Kelso Pharma is a European group with a portfolio of around 14 medicines, mainly for endocrine, gastrointestinal and central nervous system conditions. They are sold through its own U.K.-based commercial infrastructure and exported to more than 30 countries globally.

Kelso Pharma is working to expand the product range to provide additional medicines. EQT said it would support the pharmaceutical company's expansion across Europe through investment in its commercial capabilities, new product launches and selective acquisitions and licensing agreements.

Kelso's management team, led by Chief Executive Officer Tom Stratford, will continue to lead the company.

"Healthcare systems across Europe are increasingly looking to specialist companies to serve patient groups that larger pharmaceutical businesses often overlook," said Mark Braganza, partner at EQT Healthcare Growth.

"With an experienced team, its own commercial infrastructure and a portfolio serving niche patient populations, Kelso has built a strong U.K.-based business with the foundations to grow as a pan-European platform."

The deal is expected to close during the first quarter of 2027, subject to customary conditions and approvals.

Write to Dominic Chopping at dominic.chopping@wsj.com

data.title: Vanke proposes extending 95% of bond repayment due December 15 by 3 years, sources say
data.description:
Embattled property developer China Vanke has proposed to repay 5% of its onshore bond principal due on December 15, while extending the remainder by three years, three people with knowledge of the matter said on Friday.

The people declined to be identified because the proposed details are not public yet.

This would be the second extension of the bond in question that matures on December 15 (CN102282715=) - with an outstanding 1.2 billion yuan ($180.33 million) - highlighting that the financial stress is far from over for one of China's best-known real estate developers.

Vanke has extended 60% of the repayments by a year for its onshore bonds that came due during the past 12 months.

With more than $50 billion in debt, Vanke is among the last major distressed firms trying to avert a default in the country's protracted property crisis, during which many of its rivals, big and small, have defaulted on their debt repayments.

A default by Vanke, which has many projects in top-tier cities, could further dampen already weak homebuyer confidence and weigh on the broader economy, which is grappling with sluggish growth and tepid consumer spending.

In the latest proposal, the company also suggested it could defer interest payments during the extension period until the new maturity date of December 15, 2029.

Vanke did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The company will hold a bondholder meeting to vote on the extension plan on December 8.

($1 = 6.6543 yuan)

data.title: Wall St futures surge as investors return from holiday
data.description:
Key points:
  • Futures up: Dow 0.89%, S&P 500 1.65%, Nasdaq 2.47%

US stock futures surged on Friday, led by contracts tied to the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 index, as investors returned from the Thanksgiving holiday with renewed appetite for beaten-down shares.

Wall Street's main indexes have swung sharply this week after Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO and Anthropic's slide below its IPO price.

AI stocks have seesawed as investors weigh more attractive valuations against persistent concerns about heavy spending on the technology.

"The recovery in stocks seems technical. The questions that caused the market panic are still unanswered," said Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB.

"If these gains can be sustained on Friday, it would suggest that enthusiasm for the AI trade is back."

At 2:13 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis (YMcv1) jumped 446 points, or 0.89%, S&P 500 E-minis rose 119 points, or 1.65%, and Nasdaq 100 E-minis surged 645.75 points, or 2.47%.

A hawkish Federal Reserve, however, remains one of the top risks for stocks. Data this week showed the US economy grew much faster than initially estimated in the third quarter, while inflation accelerated further in October, reinforcing expectations of a rate hike.

Traders are pricing in a 99% chance of a rate hike next month, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

Wall Street was closed on Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday.
